findings.reason: the done-when's "at most one `rev-parse` per distinct repository" is reachable only if the field order is changed, because a per-path memo keyed on each pointer's distinct `worktree` yields one `rev-parse` per pointer, so the plan must state the reorder as part of the deliverable rather than as existing behaviour.
findings.text: §54 presents the `repo`-before-`worktree` resolution as current behaviour ("`claim_repository` resolves through the pointer's recorded `repo` before its `worktree`"), but `_WORKTREE_REPOSITORY_FIELDS` is `("worktree", "repo")` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1362`), so the code resolves through the worktree first, exactly as the preceding sentence says; the reorder is a change the deliverable never states

findings.reason: a worker that builds §55 before §50 has landed must invent the node-local directory §50 will use, and two independently chosen directories make §55's "beside the roadmap snapshot of §50" false as built; declaring `s55` depends on `s50` (or naming the directory in §55) settles it.
findings.text: §55 persists its index "on node-local storage that every process on the node shares, beside the roadmap snapshot of §50" and invalidates it against "another code stamp", but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 9) carries no entry for `s55`, so nothing orders §55 against §50 and §55 never names the shared directory itself

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every named symbol resolves to its cited file: `_repository_scope_claims` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:275`), `_pointer_scope_entries` (`:230`), `claim_disposition` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1500`), `claim_repository` (`:1415`), `repository_identity` (`:1390`), `_build_store_indexes` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:811`), `_store_indexes` (`:853`); the "near line" figures for `unintegrated_claim_work` (1468∈1427+), `_record_with_merged_answers` (488∈455+) and `overdue_unreconciled_runs` (`reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py`: 311∈292+) each land inside the function they name.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §54 and §55 each carry a measurable done-when with a declared negative control whose arm is distinguishable from the head arm (§54 counts `git` subprocesses and asserts the control raises the count to ≥1 per pointer; §55 counts index parses and asserts the control makes the add case parse 301 rather than 1).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections write their fragments under `docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/` (the directory exists and holds peer fragments) and require each arm's log to name its revision and end in `EXIT=`, not a scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames and helpers are named by mechanism (`test_a_dispatch_asks_git_only_about_claims_that_could_meet_its_own.py`, `test_the_review_store_index_re_reads_only_what_changed.py`), and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §54's deliverable states as a fact about the existing code that `claim_repository` "resolves through the pointer's recorded `repo` before its `worktree`", while the code it cites is `_WORKTREE_REPOSITORY_FIELDS = ("worktree", "repo")` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1362`), worktree first, and the sentence immediately before it correctly says the `rev-parse` runs "in the pointer's worktree ... today". The mechanism still produces the done-when, but only if the reader infers an unstated field reorder.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §54 is the dispatch claim-read cost and §55 the review-store index incrementality; neither carries a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §55 places its persisted index on the node-local store "beside the roadmap snapshot of §50" and gates it on "another code stamp", but no `depends-on` edge for s55 (or s54) appears in `plan-section-depends-on`, so nothing orders §55 against §50 or fixes the shared directory.
